claim: For every integer \(b\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0,2\}\), the integral evolution algebra \(E_b\) with \(e_1^2=-b e_1+e_2\), \(e_2^2=e_1\), and \(e_1e_2=0\) remains perfect modulo every prime; for unramified primes, the densities of reductions with 3, 1, and 0 nonzero idempotents are respectively \(1/6,1/2,1/3\) when \(4b^3-27\) is nonsquare, and the densities with 3 and 0 are \(1/3,2/3\) when it is a square.
integrity: Proof is algebraic plus the standard Chebotarev density theorem; no finite computation is used to infer an infinite-prime density.
scientific_limitations: The classification is for the one-parameter family E_b, not arbitrary integral evolution algebras.
The Frobenius factorization statement excludes the finite set of primes dividing the cubic discriminant; this does not affect natural densities.
The earlier preprint arXiv:2505.01444 was not directly inspected; its cited rational example was read through the later survey.
title: Prime-density classification for idempotents in a perfect integral evolution-algebra family
